docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Write your analysis in Markdown → save to input_reports/report-name-DDmonYYYY.md

2. Add YAML frontmatter at the top of the file:

---
title: "Market Sage — Stock Action Plan"
date: 2026-06-09
category: action-plan
tags: [indian-equities, portfolio, zerodha]
description: "Phased deployment plan for ₹5L fresh capital across 7 new positions."
tickers: [COFORGE, NAVINFLUOR, CAMS, LALPATHLAB]
---

3. Run /generate-report-index — copies the report to docs/reports/, updates this index page, and rebuilds the site nav.

4. git add -A && git commit -m "add report" && git push — GitHub Actions deploys to gh-pages automatically.

docs.title: LIC Shareholding Policy
docs.text: Per explicit analytical policy: LIC (Life Insurance Corporation of India) shareholding is not cited or used as a governance signal. docs.title: ⚠ Critical Context — MCX's Unique Structure
docs.text:
Three structural facts that make MCX unlike any other Indian stock:

  1. Zero promoter holding — MCX has no promoter. Original promoter FTIL (63 Moons) was ordered by SEBI to divest after the 2013 NSEL payment default. FTIL has fully exited. MCX is 100% institutionally/publicly held — zero promoter diversion risk.
  2. SEBI-regulated Market Infrastructure Institution (MII) — Board composition, risk management, technology, and governance are under continuous SEBI oversight. Strongest form of oversight for any listed entity.
  3. NSEL legacy is resolved — MCX was a separate entity from NSEL. MCX has been cleared of direct culpability. The historical overhang contributed to the 2014-2022 trough but is no longer a live issue.

docs.title: 1.3 Governance Score: STRONG
docs.text: MCX has the strongest possible governance profile for an Indian listed company: no promoter (zero fund-diversion risk), direct SEBI oversight as an MII, professional board, planned auditor rotation. The only structural consideration is the "no strategic anchor" risk — absence of a committed long-term promoter could create strategic drift or M&A vulnerability (mitigated by SEBI's approval power over exchanges).

docs.text: Item Detail Sector / Industry Capital Markets / Exchange Infrastructure Market Cap (₹Cr) ₹71,895 Cr (Large Cap) Business Model Fee-based exchange — transaction charges (% of ADTV), membership fees, tech/connectivity fees, interest on regulatory capital. Revenue = ADTV × rate (bps). Operating leverage is extreme: 107% revenue growth → 138% PAT growth in FY26. Market Position National monopoly — 95.9%+ market share in non-agri commodity derivatives (FY24) Key Commodities Gold (43% of futures), Silver (34%), Crude Oil (7%), Natural Gas (7%), Copper (7%), Base Metals (2%) Active Clients 20.9 lakh traded clients (FY26, up 61% YoY from 13.0 lakh); 4.65 crore UCCs total Economic Moat Wide — Regulatory licence (SEBI) + network effect (liquidity attracts liquidity) + switching costs Technology Project Udaan (MCX × TCS × Deutsche Boerse T7 platform) completed FY24 — the engine behind the FY25-26 volume surge Competition BSE and NSE have not built meaningful commodity market share. NCDEX limited to agri.

docs.title: Hard Reject Check: PASS — No triggers
Context-Adjusted MRS: 🟡 AMBER (both flags explained by verified one-time events)
docs.text:
Flag 1 — DSO-Revenue Divergence FY24 (Tool: Red) - DSO jumped from 10 → 33 days in FY24; tool flagged 230pp divergence - Explanation: MCX's platform migration (Oct 2023) temporarily disrupted settlement/receivables cycles. SEBI halted the migration due to technical issues; the transition window created short-term receivable pile-up. - Evidence: DSO recovered to 9 days (FY25) and 17 days (FY26) — no sustained pattern. Systematic manipulation would show persistent elevation. - Verdict: ✅ One-time operational disruption. Not a revenue manipulation signal.

Flag 2 — CWIP Aging FY22-23 (Tool: Red) - CWIP was 37.8% of fixed assets (FY22) and 53% (FY23) - Explanation: Exactly Project Udaan — MCX contracted TCS in 2022 to build the T7 trading platform. CWIP of ₹95 Cr (FY22) and ₹169 Cr (FY23) is the platform under construction. - Evidence: CWIP fell to ₹16 Cr in FY24 upon capitalization — asset was completed and deployed. - Verdict: ✅ Confirmed infrastructure investment with documented completion. Not stalled CWIP.

docs.text: At ₹2,825 with 13% discount rate and 5% terminal growth: market implies ~25-30% sustained PAT growth for 5-7 years. MCX's 5Y historical PAT CAGR is 49% — so the embedded expectations are actually below demonstrated performance. This argues the valuation is not stretched relative to history.
